messages:
Jae Park: Heads up — electron sample app on Windows is dropping the request id after an auth retry. Repro attached.

Jae Park: Steps to repro:
```
1) Start sample-app on Windows (Electron 19)
2) Turn on retries: export SAMPLEAPP_RETRIES=1
3) Force 401 on first request (dev-auth-proxy)
4) Observe logs from the app and the outgoing http headers
```

Jae Park: Observed outgoing headers in debug logs (two traceparent headers):
```
Outgoing headers: {
  "traceparent": "00-11111111111111111111111111111111-2222222222222222-01",
  "traceparent": "00-33333333333333333333333333333333-4444444444444444-01",
  "x-request-id": "req_abc123"
}
```

Lin Chen: Hmm — two traceparent headers look wrong. Could the retry middleware be re-attaching headers without deduping? On Windows header casing/merge can differ.

Samira Patel: Is the issue that our redactor sees two traceparent headers and scrubs both, then downstream code uses x-request-id which gets removed by a later redaction pass? Any log lines showing [REDACTED] where we expected the id?

Jae Park: Yup, log shows:
```
INFO Request outgoing headers: { traceparent: [REDACTED], traceparent: [REDACTED], x-request-id: [REDACTED] }
```
So the x-request-id is also getting redacted because our redaction regex matches parts of the header after the merge.

Lin Chen: Which redactor are we using in the sample app? Is this our loghook or electron's built-in scrub?

Jae Park: It's our devex-loghook included in the sample app. It runs after the http client and does a simple header redaction regex: `/authorization|traceparent|set-cookie/i`.

Marek Novak: Looks like a race: retry middleware duplicates traceparent, redactor collapses headers into a single string, regex eats adjacent tokens and eats x-request-id. On Windows the header joiner uses comma+space, we get `'traceparent: val, traceparent: val2, x-request-id: req'` and our regex with global flag ends up matching across the comma.

devex-bot: ISSUE CREATED — #4822 telemetry: duplicate traceparent on retry causes redaction to remove x-request-id (assigned to @Marek)

Marek Novak: For immediate mitigation, change redactor to only remove header values, not adjacent tokens. E.g. replace with:
```
// naive -> bad
line = line.replace(/(traceparent|authorization)[:\s]*[^,\n]+/ig, '[REDACTED]')

// safer
line = line.replace(/(traceparent|authorization)[:\s]*([^,\n]+)/ig, '$1: [REDACTED]')
```

Lin Chen: Alternatively we can dedupe headers earlier in the http client: prefer first traceparent, drop subsequent. Can add a small helper in node-fetch wrapper.

Samira Patel: Also add an integration test in sampleapps/telemetry to simulate retry+header-merge on Win and assert x-request-id preserved.

Jae Park: I'll send a PR with the safer redactor change + a note in the sample app README. Also enabling DEBUG_TELEMETRY_ORDER=1 for local repro.

otel-bot: NOTE — otel-js propagator behavior on Windows noted in upstream issue: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/issues/999

Marek Novak: Thanks all. I'll pick up the issue, add a small patch to sample app and make the redactor change in devex-loghook. @Samira please add the integration test when you have cycles.

Samira Patel: ack :thumbsup:

Jae Park: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/321 (contains repro + redactor fix)

Lin Chen: Nice. After PR lands let's run a quick canary on Dedicated to validate no customer-facing noise.

Jae Park: Will do. Thanks folks :rocket:
